items.title: Gene Bertoncini interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 13, 2001
items.q: I was really upset to visit the Frank Lloyd Wright office and school in Taliesin Arizona

ctx.x: I knew that’s what you were referring to. No I have a degree in architecture. I fell in love with architecture. I used to copy the plans out of the New York Times Sunday real estate section. And I did some work in construction. My dad always — he rebuilt two homes when we were growing up and so I was always like kind of interested in the building stuff. I always thought I might be in that area. And my high school advisor said — well when I told him I liked, I also liked drafting. In those days we actually drew…
such — to have that white piece of paper and the tools to draw with, to make lines. That was very nice. I enjoyed that a lot. I still would enjoy that too.
